title: The "tie-down": one sentence for any objection
creator: Brian Ron Mark (@therealbrianmark)
summary: When a prospect raises an objection, first confirm it's the only thing in the way: "So if it weren't for that, you'd want to move forward, is that right?" A yes isolates the objection, so you solve just that one problem and close. A "well, also…" tells you there's a hidden objection to find first.
takeaways: Isolate an objection before you answer it.
If the tie-down gets a "well, also…", find the real objection before solving anything.
For us, book the install instead of pushing for "today": a pressured yes cancels.

lessons.title: Isolate any objection before you answer it (tie-down)
lessons.how: Repeat the objection back and ask if it's the only barrier. Yes means you know exactly what to solve. "Well, also…" means there's a hidden objection, so find it before solving the first one. End on "is that right?" to get a real "that's right".
say: So if it weren't for [the objection], you'd want to get it set up. Is that right?
lessons.builds_on: Summarize until they say "that's right", then present

example.setting: Door knock in a newly released town. The homeowner likes the idea but hesitates.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: It sounds good, but I'm locked in with Optimum.

lines.speaker: Rep
lines.text: Totally get it. So if it weren't for the contract, you'd want fiber at the house. Is that right?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Well... also I heard installs take forever and they tear up the yard.

lines.speaker: Rep
lines.text: Glad you said that. Let's talk about the install first: [fill in: install process and timeline]. Then we'll figure out the contract.

lessons.title: Price: tie it down, then right-size the plan
lessons.how: Confirm price is the only issue, then solve just that by offering the plan that fits. Don't discount or invent promos.
say: If this fit the budget, you'd want to get on the install calendar. Is that right?

example.setting: Outbound call. The customer likes fiber but says it's more than they pay now.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: I want it, but that's more than I'm paying now.

lines.speaker: Rep
lines.text: Completely fair. So if it fit the budget, you'd want to get on the install calendar. Is that right?

lines.speaker: Rep
lines.text: Then let's look at [fill in: lowest plan and price]. It still gives you fiber, just at a speed that fits a smaller budget.

lessons.title: "I need to talk to my spouse": tie it down, then get both
lessons.how: Confirm the spouse is the only open question, then make it easy to include them: a call-back when both are home, or book the install now so they can share it.
say: If they're on board, is this something you'd want for the house?

example.setting: Door knock on a weeknight. One spouse answers.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: I'd have to talk to my husband first.

lines.speaker: Rep
lines.text: Of course. If he's on board, is this something you'd want for the house?

lines.speaker: Rep
lines.text: Great. When are you both usually home? I can call back then and answer his questions directly.

objections.objection: I don't have the money / over budget
objections.response: Tie it down, then offer the plan that fits [fill in: what reps can offer].

objections.objection: I need to talk to my spouse / no time
objections.response: Named in the reel as objections the tie-down works on; the fix (call back with both) is ours.

applies.inbound: Callers who hesitate usually have one specific worry. Isolating it keeps the call from ending in "let me think about it."
applies.outbound: Turns a vague brush-off into a specific problem, or reveals there isn't one.
applies.door_to_door: Fits "I need to ask my spouse" best: isolate, then book a time when both are home.

doesnt_fit.why: A pressured "today" yes is the one that cancels before install. Book the install instead.
Overclaim: some objections are real and final (can't get service, moving, no budget). The tie-down tells you which ones those are.
His product, not ours. Only offer what our plans allow [fill in].

drill.goal: For each objection, isolate it with a tie-down ending in "is that right?", and only then solve it.
drill.customer_script: Cycle through "it's too expensive," "I need to talk to my husband," and "I'm under contract with Optimum." On one, answer the tie-down with "well, also…" and add a second worry, like slow installs.
drill.debrief: Did the rep catch the hidden second objection before solving the first? Did they push "today," or book the install?
